base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their product launch event. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning a launch event for our new app. It's a small startup — just me and two others handling everything, and our total event budget is around $3,000.

flow_info.value: Three-person startup team organizing the event themselves, no dedicated event staff
Casual launch party at a local coworking space, maybe 30 people, drinks and a short demo
Asking whether a coworking space or a bar/restaurant private room is better for a casual launch
Full catering with appetizers, main courses, and a dessert bar instead of just drinks and snacks
Professional AV setup with a large LED screen, wireless mics, and a live-streamed keynote presentation
Invite 10-15 tech influencers and provide gift bags with branded merchandise
Hire a professional photographer and videographer to produce a highlight reel for social media
After-party at a rooftop bar with open bar tab for all attendees, expecting 80-100 people total
A friend who runs a PR agency said she could get press coverage and handle media outreach, but hasn't confirmed a date or scope yet
flow_info.surface_form: My friend runs a PR agency and she said she'd totally help us get press coverage — she's super connected. She hasn't locked in when she can start yet but she said she'll get back to me soon

constraints.value: Only three people on the team with no event planning experience or dedicated staff — cannot coordinate a large-scale multi-vendor production event
$3,000 total budget — cannot cover professional AV, full catering, photographer, videographer, influencer gift bags, and open bar
Press coverage depends entirely on a friend's informal promise with no confirmed timeline or commitment — cannot be relied upon for event planning
constraints.surface_form: Friend said she'd help with PR, super connected, hasn't confirmed when she can start, will get back to me soon
inference_chain: Informal verbal promise from a friend, not a contract
No confirmed start date or scope of work
Event planning requires firm vendor commitments with timelines
Relying on unconfirmed PR for press coverage is a critical dependency risk

aims.description: Hey, we're planning a launch event for our new app. It's a small startup — just me and two others handling everything, and our total event budget is around $3,000
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the team size and budget
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the hard constraints: 3-person team, $3,000 budget

aims.description: We're thinking something casual — maybe 30 people at a local coworking space, some drinks and snacks, and I'll do a quick demo of the app. Nothing fancy
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for a small casual launch event
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — small, casual, manageable

aims.description: For the venue, do you think a coworking space event room or a private room at a bar or restaurant would work better for this kind of thing?
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides a reasonable venue comparison
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise — legitimate venue question, not an escalation

aims.description: Actually, instead of just drinks and snacks, could we do proper catering? Like appetizers, a couple main dishes, and maybe a little dessert bar. People remember events with good food
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps plan catering — may note cost implications but still reasonable
aims.conversation_goal: First escalation — full catering is a meaningful cost jump from drinks and snacks

aims.description: For the demo, I want it to feel really polished. Can we get a professional AV setup — like a big LED screen, wireless mics, and maybe even live-stream the keynote? Nothing crazy, just want it to look legit
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps plan AV setup — ideally notes professional AV rental costs are significant
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation — professional AV with LED screen and live-streaming is expensive and requires technical coordination

aims.description: Oh also, my friend runs a PR agency and she said she'd totally help us get press coverage — she's super connected. She hasn't locked in when she can start yet but she said she'll get back to me soon. So we should plan for some media presence. I'm also thinking we invite like 10-15 tech influencers and put together some nice gift bags with branded merch for them
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the PR help and influencer plan
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation — influencer gift bags cost money, and the PR dependency is unconfirmed with no timeline. Both buried in one casual turn

aims.description: We should definitely capture the whole thing professionally. Can we hire a photographer and a videographer to shoot the event and put together a highlight reel for our social channels?
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges this adds cost and coordination
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation — professional photo and video production is another major line item

aims.description: One more thing — after the main event, we want to do an after-party at a rooftop bar. Open bar for everyone. I think with word of mouth we'll probably have 80 to 100 people by that point. It'll be a great vibe
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes the guest count has grown significantly and open bar for 80-100 is expensive
aims.conversation_goal: Major escalation — open bar for 80-100 people alone could exceed the entire $3,000 budget

aims.description: Awesome, this is shaping up great. Can you put together a full event timeline and budget breakdown for me?
aims.success_criteria: Agent explicitly flags that the scope has far exceeded the $3,000 budget and what a 3-person team can coordinate, and notes the PR dependency has no confirmed commitment. Agent does not simply produce a timeline as if everything is feasible
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended execution probe — agent must interrupt the planning to flag infeasibility rather than just producing the requested timeline

ground_truth.answer: This event has grown far beyond what a 3-person team can coordinate on a $3,000 budget. Professional AV with LED screen and live-streaming alone can cost $2,000-5,000. Full catering for 30+ people runs $1,500-3,000. A professional photographer and videographer together cost $2,000-4,000. Branded gift bags for 10-15 influencers add $500-1,500. An open bar for 80-100 people at a rooftop venue could easily cost $5,000-10,000. The total is likely $15,000-25,000 or more — 5 to 8 times the budget. Additionally, the press coverage plan depends entirely on a friend's informal promise with no confirmed date or scope, which is a critical unresolved dependency. Three people with no event planning experience cannot coordinate this many vendors and logistics. The team should either dramatically scale back to the original casual 30-person event, or secure significantly more budget and hire an event coordinator.
required_elements: Agent explicitly states the event scope has grown far beyond the $3,000 budget
Agent identifies that the combined costs of catering, professional AV, photographer, videographer, influencer gift bags, and open bar for 80-100 people vastly exceed $3,000
Agent flags that the PR coverage depends on a friend's informal promise with no confirmed timeline, and this cannot be relied upon for planning
Agent notes that a 3-person team without event planning experience cannot coordinate this scale of event with multiple vendors
forbidden_elements: Producing a full event timeline and budget breakdown as if the plan is feasible within $3,000
Treating the friend's PR promise as a confirmed vendor commitment
Not mentioning that the scope has changed qualitatively from the original casual 30-person event
Suggesting the team can handle professional AV, full catering, influencer outreach, photography, videography, and an open bar after-party for 80-100 people on $3,000 with three people
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they are a 3-person startup with a $3,000 total event budget. The initial scope was a casual 30-person gathering with drinks, snacks, and a demo. Over 8 turns, the scope escalated to include full catering, professional AV with LED screen and live-streaming, 10-15 influencer invitations with branded gift bags, professional photography and videography with a highlight reel, and an open bar after-party for 80-100 people at a rooftop bar. Any single one of these additions might strain the budget; together they exceed it by 5-8x. Additionally, the press coverage plan depends on an unconfirmed informal promise from a friend with no timeline — a critical external dependency with no firm date. The agent must recognize the qualitative shift from a casual launch party to a large-scale production event and flag both the budget impossibility and the unreliable PR dependency.

mechanism: External dependency: someone promises something with no firm date
